claims.text: Arthrocentesis for any joint effusion: synovial WBC with differential, Gram stain and cultures, and polarized-light microscopy for crystals.
claims.quote: Joint aspiration (arthrocentesis) for synovial fluid examination should be performed in patients with joint effusion (see How to Do Arthrocentesis). Synovial fluid examination includes white blood cell (WBC) count with differential, Gram stain and cultures, and microscopic examination for crystals using polarized light.
claims.locator: Pain in and Around a Single Joint, Testing

claims.text: Crystals confirm crystal arthritis but do not exclude a coexisting infection.
claims.quote: Finding crystals in synovial fluid confirms crystal-induced arthritis but does not exclude coexisting infection.
claims.locator: Pain in and Around a Single Joint, Testing

claims.text: Serum urate should not be used to diagnose gout; ESR, CRP and fever do not reliably separate septic arthritis from other causes.
claims.quote: Serum urate level should not be used to diagnose gout because it is neither sensitive nor specific and does not necessarily reflect the presence of intra-articular uric acid deposits. Elevated ESR and/or CRP (or the presence or absence of fever) do not accurately distinguish septic arthritis from other etiologies of arthritis.
claims.locator: Pain in and Around a Single Joint, Testing

claims.text: Radiographs rarely change the diagnosis in acute monoarthritis unless fracture or osteomyelitis is suspected.
claims.quote: Radiographs rarely change the diagnosis in acute monarthritis unless fracture or osteomyelitis is suspected.
claims.locator: Pain in and Around a Single Joint, Testing

claims.text: Polyarthritis: arthrocentesis, usually ESR and CRP, serologic testing, and radiographs and/or ultrasound when chronic.
claims.quote: The following tests are particularly important: Arthrocentesis Usually erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) Serologic testing In chronic arthritis, radiographs and/or ultrasound

claims.text: Serologies when a systemic inflammatory disorder is suspected: ANA, double-stranded DNA, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP and ANCA, ordered to support a specific diagnosis (SLE, ANCA vasculitis, RA).
claims.quote: Once a diagnosis of a systemic inflammatory disorder is clinically suspected, supportive serologic testing for antinuclear antibodies, double-stranded DNA, rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) may assist in making the diagnosis. Specific tests should only be ordered to provide support for a specific diagnosis, such as systemic lupus erythematosus, ANCA-associated vasculitis, or rheumatoid arthritis.

claims.text: Chronic arthritis: radiographs and/or ultrasound for joint damage (eg, erosions in RA).
claims.quote: If arthritis is chronic, radiographs and/or ultrasound are typically done to look for signs of joint damage (eg, erosions in rheumatoid arthritis).
